attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway so node3 has a single, stable gateway address (10.10.13.254) to reach node4's network, preferring node1 while healthy and failing over to node2 when node1 is down. node1/eth1/node2/eth1/node3-enp8s0 form LAN-A (10.10.13.0/24, VRRP vrid 51, VIP .254); node1/eth2/node2/eth2/node4-enp8s0 form LAN-B (10.10.14.0/24, VRRP vrid 52, VIP .254). node1 has priority 200 (preferred master), node2 has priority 100 (backup). node3 and node4 each got a static IP and a specific route to the other's subnet via their local VRRP VIP, configured through Ansible (community.general.nmcli) from node5 (control_node), with VyOS routers configured via ansible.builtin.shell driving the native `configure/set/commit/save` CLI. All work was done with root/vyos SSH keyed via CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY (VyOS's own `system login user ... public-keys` config, since manual authorized_keys edits get reconciled away on VyOS boot). Failover was demonstrated live (disabling node1's links made node2 take MASTER within seconds with zero ping loss to node4 from node3), and preemption back to node1 was confirmed. All 5 nodes (node1–node5) were then restarted one at a time (VRRP backup covering node1/node2 reboots, quorum/health checked before proceeding), each with a changed OS boot_id proving a real restart, and each recovered its configuration/services: VyOS VRRP state and interface config persisted and rejoined correctly, RHEL NetworkManager static IP/route persisted, and the Ansible control node's playbook/inventory/SSH key persisted and a re-run confirmed full idempotency (changed=0 across all hosts) plus continued node3↔node4 connectivity via the single VRRP gateway.
